newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan bourse head sees privatisation by February.
newsitem.headline: Milan bourse head sees privatisation by February.

text.p: Plans to privatise the Milan stock market could be finalised by next February, Enzo Berlanda, chairman of the Italian bourse regulator Consob, said.

"By the end of February we will have one or more private companies able to run the markets with Consob, which will keep only the principal powers of authority," he told the industry commission of the lower house Senate.
Ahead of the privatisation of the Italian financial markets, a company has been set up to oversee the restructuring of the markets to make them more competitive.

Sint SpA, formed by 22 main brokerage houses and banks and with capital of 44 billion lire, will act as purchaser of the stock, bond and derivatives markets to be privatised under the Eurosim directive.

Berlanda, in reply to a Senate commission query on ways to increase the efficiency and transparency of the stock market, said the idea of getting companies to issue quarterly financial reports was still a long way off.

He said Consob was carrying out informal soundings of the main quoted companies on the feasibility of making their three-monthly results available to the market, "but we are still a long way off from being able to achieve this."
